question: In India, in the sphere of law making, a Bill does not become an Act unless it receives the assent of the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In India, a Bill passed by both the **Houses of Parliament **becomes an** Act** only after the **President **gives his **assent** to it.
 
• The Bill **does not** become law if the Governor or the President, as the case may be,** withholds** his assent.
 
• The President is the **head of the Indian state** and exercises his powers and functions through various **constitutional offices and authorities**, including the power to give assent to Bills passed by Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Attorney General** is the **chief legal advisor **to the government of India and provides legal advice to the government on various matters.
 
• The **Prime Minister **is the head of the government of India and exercises **executive powers.**
 
• The** Vice President **is the second-highest constitutional office in India and acts as the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha.**
